value.name: introduce payment schedule item
value.description: Asha raises the fourth agenda item, which concerns how the charge will be paid over time.
evidence: "Item four," Asha said. "The schedule of payment on the charge."

value.name: frame payment as family decision
value.description: The narration explains that drafting the payment terms forces the family to decide what kind of family they will be.
evidence: This was the item that had taken her the longest to draft, because it was the item in which the family had to decide, in numbers, what kind of family they were going to try to be.

value.name: reveal Daniel needs money
value.description: Asha recalls that Daniel needs money and that she understood his need without judging him for it.
evidence: He had told her that on the second day, in the kitchen, without quite telling her that, and she had understood, and she had not held it against him, because need was not a character flaw, although the things people did because of it sometimes were.

value.name: establish Lucia lacks cash
value.description: The scene states that Lucia cannot pay a third of the appraised value in cash and that no one expects her to.
evidence: Lucia did not have a third of the appraised value in cash. No one in the room expected her to.

value.name: negotiate payment terms
value.description: The family focuses on how long the charge will take to pay, under what terms, and with what security.
evidence: The question was over how long a period, on what terms, and with what security, the charge would be paid.

value.name: exchange competing proposals
value.description: Daniel, Lucia, and Asha each have proposals, and they have been trading them by email over the weekend.
evidence: Daniel had a proposal. Lucia had a proposal. Asha had a proposal.

They had exchanged these over email through the weekend, and the proposals had begun very far apart and ended, by Sunday night, within shouting distance of one another, and the purpose of this morning was to close the remaining distance.
value.time_hint: through the weekend; by Sunday night; this morning

value.name: ask Daniel to explain position
value.description: Asha invites Daniel to explain where he stands on the payment arrangement.
evidence: "Daniel," Asha said. "Walk us through where you are."

value.name: Daniel speaks calmly
value.description: Daniel explains his position for several minutes without raising his voice.
evidence: He did. He spoke for perhaps four minutes. He did not raise his voice.

value.name: Daniel abandons combative language
value.description: Asha notices that Daniel no longer uses the entitled, adversarial phrases he used earlier in the dispute.
evidence: He did not, Asha noticed, use any of the phrases he had used in the first week: not "what I am owed," not "by right," not "before anyone else gets clever."

value.name: Daniel reflects on his position
value.description: Daniel says he has spent the week thinking about the matter, indicating a shift toward deliberation.
evidence: He said he had thought about it over the week
